hints: Start by classifying each alcohol as primary, secondary or tertiary, since that controls what they can do.
Notice that butan-1-ol is primary, butan-2-ol is secondary, and 2-methylbutan-2-ol with three alkyl groups on the C-OH carbon is tertiary.
Recall which class resists oxidation by acidified dichromate because it has no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the OH group.
walkthrough:
**Classify the three alcohols**

Think of the carbon attached to OH. How many other carbons is it joined to? That tells you the class.

$$\text{butan-1-ol: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH (primary, 1}^\circ\text{)}$$ $$\text{butan-2-ol: CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (secondary, 2}^\circ\text{)}$$ $$\text{2-methylbutan-2-ol: CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (tertiary, 3}^\circ\text{)}$$

**Check the reactions all alcohols share**

All alcohols, whether 1, 2 or 3 degrees, have an OH group that can form esters, release hydrogen with sodium, and lose water to form an alkene.

$$\text{R-OH + HCOOH} \rightarrow \text{HCOOR + H}_2\text{O}$$ $$\text{2ROH + 2Na} \rightarrow \text{2RONa + H}_2$$ $$\text{R-CH-C(OH)-R} \rightarrow \text{alkene + H}_2\text{O}$$

**Check oxidation to a carbonyl**

Oxidation needs at least one H on the C-OH carbon to remove. Primary gives an aldehyde then acid, secondary gives a ketone, but tertiary has no such H so it is not oxidised.

$$\text{primary: RCH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{RCHO} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}$$ $$\text{secondary: R}_2\text{CHOH} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C=O (ketone)}$$ $$\text{tertiary: R}_3\text{COH} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$

**Pick the not correct statement**

Since 2-methylbutan-2-ol cannot be oxidised to a carbonyl, the claim that they all can be oxidised is false. That is the statement that is not correct.

options.A: This is a correct statement, so not the answer. All alcohols undergo esterification with a carboxylic acid like methanoic acid in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, regardless of being primary, secondary or tertiary.
options.B: This is a correct statement, so not the answer. All alcohols react with sodium to form a sodium alkoxide and hydrogen gas, because the O-H bond is present in every case.
options.C: This is a correct statement, so not the answer. All three can be dehydrated with hot concentrated sulfuric acid or hot aluminium oxide to give an alkene, butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol give butene isomers and 2-methylbutan-2-ol gives methylbutene.
options.D: This is the not correct statement, so it is the answer. Butan-1-ol oxidises to butanal then butanoic acid, and butan-2-ol oxidises to butanone, but 2-methylbutan-2-ol is tertiary with no H on the C-OH carbon and resists oxidation by acidified potassium dichromate.
